haiku-low.q1: Step 5, after preflight and before the new colour starts, once per deploy. The live release must keep working, since migrations are additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a contract migration whose header names the commit that removed the last use; it runs only if the live release contains that commit.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new targets must pass three consecutive /healthz checks, then smoke tests and pre-switch check. If not by T0+10 min, Abort with health_timeout.
haiku-low.q4: At step 11, one call repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one, then reads it back to confirm.
haiku-low.q5: 5xx above 1% in any watch evaluation, or 3 unreadable-metrics evaluations in a row. Rollback repoints to old colour, stops new, pauses deploys; migrations stay.
haiku-low.q6: Until retire_at, 30 minutes after the switch, the listener can be repointed. After that, rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release via catalog-web-redeploy.
haiku-low.q7: Earlier migrations stay applied, the failed one rolls back, and any invalid index needs a fix-forward drop. Abort runs; live colour and listener are untouched.
haiku-low.q8: Listener's forward target is the source of truth. deploy-state.json's live_colour mirrors it, checked each step; the other colour gets the release.
haiku-low.q9: A lock in deploy-state.json, taken by conditional write only when empty and unpaused. Held until the deploy ends, about 40-45 minutes on success.
haiku-low.q10: A test listener on port 8443, reachable only from the CI network, forwards to the new colour's target group. Public listener is untouched until the switch.
haiku-low.q11: The new image's migrate command, as a one-off job against PostgreSQL. Its advisory lock stops overlap; its history table skips applied migrations.
haiku-low.q12: New-colour instances are deregistered with a 30 s drain, stopped, and marked off. Next deploy's preflight stops any leftovers.

sonnet.q1: Step 5, after preflight and before the test listener and starting the new colour. The live (old) release must keep working against the migrated schema; migrations are additive, so it is unaffected. Contract migrations run only if the live release contains the contract-after commit.
sonnet.q2: Only via a contract migration with a header `-- contract-after: <commit-sha>` naming the commit that removed the last use. The pipeline runs it only if the live release contains that commit (checked in the PR check and again at step 4).
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must be healthy in the load balancer's target health (three consecutive /healthz passes), and smoke tests must pass, within 10 minutes of T0. If not, Abort runs with reason health_timeout (or smoke_failed). The public listener is never touched.
sonnet.q4: In step 11, after a conditional write sets step: switching, a single call changes the public listener's forward target from the old target group to the new one. The pipeline reads the listener back to confirm. It then records T-switch and sets the colour statuses (new live, old standby).
sonnet.q5: Triggers: the 5xx rate above 1% in any evaluation (5xx_breach), metrics unreadable for 3 evaluations in a row (metrics_unavailable), or an engineer running catalog-web-rollback. Rollback sets step rolling_back, repoints the public listener to the old colour, sets live_colour to old and old status live, records outcome rolled_back, stops the new colour (status off), sets paused true, releases the lock and pages on-call. It leaves migrations in place (never reversed). The old colour stays live.
sonnet.q6: Until retire_at, which is T-switch + 30 minutes (the rollback job is refused once step is retiring). After that, a problem is handled by a redeploy of the previous release with catalog-web-redeploy <release-sha>. It refuses releases older than an applied contract migration's contract-after commit.
sonnet.q7: The failed migration's transaction rolls back. Earlier successful migrations in the run stay applied (additive, so the live release is unaffected). A failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY leaves an invalid index that the fix-forward migration must drop. Abort runs with reason migration_failed. No new instances have started and the listener is untouched. The lock is released, deploys are not paused, and the fix is a new merge.
sonnet.q8: The public listener's forward target on the load balancer is the source of truth. It is mirrored in live_colour in catalog-web/deploy-state.json, in the deploy-state bucket. Step 4 records from_colour and to_colour (the other colour) in the deploy record there, after checking that the listener matches live_colour.
sonnet.q9: A lock in deploy-state.json, taken through a conditional (versioned) write in step 3. It is held until the deploy ends: after the old colour is retired, or after an abort or rollback. A successful deploy holds it roughly 40-45 minutes.
sonnet.q10: Through a test listener on the same load balancer, port 8443, reachable only from the CI network. It forwards to the new colour's target group, while the public listener still points at the old colour.
sonnet.q11: Step 5 runs the new image's migrate command as a one-off job against PostgreSQL. The migration tool's database advisory lock stops runs from overlapping. The history table records applied migrations, so only pending ones run. Step 5 happens once per deploy, and after a job restart, migrations already in the history table are not re-run.
sonnet.q12: On abort, the new colour's instances are deregistered and stopped, and the colour is set to status off, release none. On rollback, they are drained for 30 s, stopped and set to off. If stopping fails, it retries for 5 minutes and then flags it. The leftover instances get no public traffic, and the next deploy's preflight (step 4) stops them and logs the event. After an abort deploys are not paused; after a rollback they are paused until catalog-web-resume-deploys.
